text:
If you’re heading out for a crisp fall afternoon, Burlington is delivering: clear skies, a northerly breeze, and a cool 57 right now. The sun should carry us to a high near 67, with that north wind occasionally noticeable but no rain threat. The lake is quiet too, with waves a foot or less, though the 63-degree water is still a bracing swim. Plan on a clear, cooler evening, temperatures sliding toward 48 with lighter wind.

Friday looks much the same, just a touch warmer, sunny with a high around 70 and a north breeze. The weekend is where the forecast gets less settled: Saturday should start dry, but showers become more possible later, with a better chance Sunday. Enjoy the outdoor window today through Friday, and bring a light layer for tonight’s waterfront plans.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): For the upcoming weekend, we continue to watch that Nor’Easter off the coast of southern New England. Right now it looks like Saturday all of us start dry, but a few showers may enter southern Vermont into that afternoon and evening. We all have a better chance at showers into the day Sunday though. Right now, the further north and west you are the less rain you see generally between .1-.3″ with southeastern portions of the area could run upwards .5″. While not a ton, it will be good news for most as rainfall deficits have been mounting in the last few months. Channel wind gusts between 25 and 35 mph are expected across the Champlain Valley and Green Mountain summits Saturday, into Sunday.
